name: Centre-right politics
summary: The centre-right, as political scientists define it, is a big-tent family of conservative and Christian democratic parties drawing together social traditionalists, market liberals and national conservatives, not a fixed policy package. Its own account in the EPP manifesto stresses subsidiarity, pluralist democracy, equal rights, the social market economy, sound public finances, NATO and controlled borders.
scope: The centre-right as Gidron and Ziblatt (2019) define it: big-tent parties of the right, most directly conservative and Christian democratic ones, as an organisational form that emerged after 1945. The EPP, which calls itself the party of the centre and the centre right, states its values in its manifestos; they answer only where presented as tenets. It excludes radical-right parties and narrower strands.
